He went again to Jinyang and received the *Sūtra of Immeasurable Life* from Master Chao. He entered meditative absorption for seven days, after which Chao requested that he observe his future place of rebirth.
Daobao replied, "Master, you must repent for three offenses before you can attain rebirth there.

Once, when installing a Buddha image, you placed it beneath the eaves and windows while you yourself stayed in a deep inner chamber; this is one offense. You must repent before the Buddha. Furthermore, once..."
"Employing ordained monks for labor—this is the second offense. It should be confessed before the Sangha of the four directions.

Furthermore, because of constructing buildings, many insect lives were destroyed—this is the third offense. It should be confessed before all sentient beings. You must contemplate your past transgressions with profound stillness and repent from the depths of your heart.
After a long time, the Way emerged from within his concentration and said to Huichao, "The Master’s offenses have been extinguished. Hereafter..."
When white light came to illuminate him, it was a sign of his rebirth in the Pure Land. While traveling and teaching in the capital, those who returned to him were as numerous as in a marketplace.
Suddenly, he fell slightly ill; he then closed his room and passed away with a serene countenance. A wondrous fragrance and celestial music arose, and he vanished toward the west.

Fahui was a native of Bingzhou. He constantly practiced the sixteen contemplations of the *Amitābha-sūtra*. Once, upon emerging from his meditation, he saw Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta appearing in the sky.
Fahui prostrated himself and wept as rain, saying, "Fortunately, by means of my physical eyes, I have been able to behold the countenances of the sages.

What I regret is that there is no one in the world to transmit this. Suddenly, two men appeared who claimed to be skilled at painting sacred images. When they had finished, both men vanished without a trace. Thereupon—
He said to his disciples, "The time has come for me to travel westward. Is there anyone who will follow me? A young boy replied, "I shall go at once by the Master’s command.
He informed his parents, returned to the monastery, bathed, and sat in the lotus posture before the image, passing away.
Huida patted his back and said, "Why have you gone ahead of me? He immediately ordered his disciples to join in chanting the Buddha's name. [The boy] looked up with his eyes.
Looking westward, all was silent and without sound.
Fachih was a native of Jiangning. Having met Chan Master Huineng of Huangmei and realized the essentials of the mind, he succeeded to the patriarchal seat of Niutou.

He constantly maintained mindfulness of the Pure Land, never deviating from it whether looking up or down. As his end approached, he instructed his disciples to leave his remains exposed beneath the pines, so that birds and beasts might [consume them].

"Eat my flesh and blood; this shall serve as the cause for the establishment of a Pure Land. The disciple followed his instructions. Then he saw dozens of divine banners coming from the west and circling the mountain;
the banners emitted a supernatural light that illuminated his chamber.
Huìrì boarded a ship and sailed to the South Sea, reaching the various kingdoms of India to seek out spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*).

He inquired which country or region was free from suffering and possessed happiness, and what dharma or practice would allow one to quickly behold the Buddha. The Tripitaka masters of India all praised the Land of Purity (*Sukhāvatī*).
Day by day he heard [the Dharma] with great joy. Upon reaching the kingdom of Gandhāra, there was an image of Avalokiteśvara on a mountain that would sometimes manifest its form to those who prayed.

For seven days, he abstained from food, vowing to end his life in order to make his request. On the night of the seventh day, Avalokiteśvara appeared in the sky with a purple-golden countenance over ten feet tall;
he stroked Riju’s head with his hand and said: "You desire to transmit the Dharma to benefit others, and you further wish to be reborn in Sukhāvatī."

"Rejoice in the Pure Land; it shall be as you have vowed. In the seventh year of the Kaiyuan era, he returned eastward and reached Chang’an, where he presented the true image of the Buddha and Sanskrit scriptures to the Emperor.
The Emperor honored his virtue by bestowing upon him the title "Tripitaka Master Cimin. He composed the *Jingtu wen* (Treatise on the Pure Land), which circulated throughout the world.
In the seventh year of the Tianbao era, as he was about to pass away, he saw a lotus flower before him, shaped like the sun’s disk.
The Dharma Master Chengyuan first studied under Master Tang in Chengdu. Upon reaching Jingzhou, he advanced his studies under Master Zhen at Yuquan.

Master Zhen entrusted him with Mount Heng, charging him to become a preeminent leader of the teaching. Those who followed him to receive transformation numbered in the tens of thousands. He had a disciple named Fazhao, who initially resided on Mount Lu;

through the stage of the *samyaktva-niyāma* (the group of those destined for rightness), he proceeded toward the Land of Peace and Bliss (*Sukhāvatī*), where he beheld [Amitābha] clad in coarse garments.
Regarding the one who attended the Buddha, the Buddha said, "It is Chengyuan of Mount Heng. When [the Emperor] went out to seek him, he found one who resembled him; thus, he followed him to study.
He propagated the teachings throughout the world. During the reign of Emperor Daizong, Fazhao served as National Teacher and spoke of his master’s extraordinary virtue.

The Son of Heaven turned southward and paid him homage. As the Master’s Way was such that it could not be sought through worldly means, the Emperor named his dwelling the "Pratyutpanna Bodhimanda" (Banzhou Daochang) to honor his station.
The Master first resided beneath a rocky cliff to the southwest of the mountain.

If people brought him food, he would eat; if they did not, he ate earth and mud and consumed herbs and trees. His manner of obtaining clothing was likewise. [He extended] as far south as the coastal frontiers of the sea, and northward...

From the distant land of Youdu, he came seeking the Way. Sometimes he encountered him at precipices and valleys, appearing with a haggard form and a soiled face, personally carrying firewood and brushwood, acting as a servant and treating him with familiarity;
yet this was the Master himself. Whenever he transformed others, he established them in the Middle Way and taught them, employing skillful means to enable them to reach the goal swiftly;
thus he manifested single-minded devotion, writing upon the streets and alleys and carving into the mountain streams and valleys, grandly inscribing and guiding them.

Supported from below, the Way was perfected without seeking; things were accomplished without speech. All people brought cloth and silk, cut wood and stone, and deposited them at the mountain entrance;
they neither resisted nor labored. Once the temple buildings were complete, an imperial edict was issued during the reign of Emperor Dezong to honor and establish it as Mida Temple.
On the nineteenth day of the seventh month in the eighteenth year of the Zhengyuan era, he passed away at the temple at the age of... (years).
91. The world ranked him as the third patriarch of the Lotus Society.
Sengxuan was a native of Bingzhou. Initially, he focused his mindfulness on Maitreya, vowing to be reborn in the Inner Court (Tuṣita Heaven). At the age of ninety, he met Master Chao.
Upon hearing the Dharma of the Pure Land, he first turned his mind toward it. Morning and evening, he performed a thousand prostrations to the Buddha and recited the Buddha’s name ten thousand times.
After three years, he fell ill and said to his disciples, "Amitābha Buddha has bestowed upon me fragrant robes; Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta have shown me their precious hands.
It is time for me to depart. Seven days after his passing, a wondrous fragrance did not dissipate. At that time, Qifang Yuan was present.
The two masters witnessed this event and, before the Avalokiteśvara statue at Wuzhen Temple, broke off a willow branch and placed it in the hand of the image, making a vow:
"If Fang and the others have a karmic affinity for the Pure Land, let this branch not wither for seven days. When the period arrived, the branch grew even more luxuriant.
Fang was indeed filled with joy; for several months he practiced mindfulness and visualization day and night without ceasing, until he suddenly felt himself standing by a pool of the seven treasures.
He entered a great jeweled pavilion and saw the Buddha and the two Great Beings seated upon jeweled lotus pedestals, their radiance shining brilliantly.
Fangguo prostrated before them. The Buddha said to him, "Recall my name, and you shall all be born in my land. He also saw jeweled banners and pearl nets;
within a precious carriage, a Brahmin monk was driving it and said to him, "I am Dharmakara. I have come specifically to welcome you. Fangguo—
Suddenly, he felt as though he were riding in a carriage moving forward. He also heard Śākyamuni Buddha and Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva praising the Pure Land with Brahma-sounds.
Within the jeweled palace, there were three paths made of precious materials: the first path consisted entirely of white-robed laypeople; the second path had a mixture of monastics and laity;
the third path was occupied solely by the monastic community. The Buddha pointed and said to Fang: "These are all..."
Those in Jambudvīpa who practice mindfulness of the Buddha shall be reborn in this land. Five days later, the two men were free from illness when they suddenly heard the sound of a bell.
Fangguo said, "The sound of the bell is our affair. At that moment, they both immediately passed away.
Biancai was a native of Xiangyang. He practiced the Pure Land teachings in secret for twenty years without ever speaking of them.
He was on intimate terms only with Ren Gong of Huru, to whom he said, "Cai will certainly be reborn in the Pure Land; my expectation is that it will happen within ten years.
Later, he instructed his disciples to inform Ren Gong, saying, "The period previously expected has already arrived. When Ren Gong reached the gate, Biancai said, "I am departing."
He passed away while sitting in the lotus posture. The multitude heard the sound of celestial music coming from the west, and an extraordinary fragrance spread everywhere.

They realized that he had been residing at the Chonglin Monastery on Mount Ping for three years, preaching the Dharma to spirits and deities, and that there had been frequent auspicious manifestations.

He had once made forty-eight vows. Through the great compassion of Avalokiteśvara, he was granted an audience with Amitābha Buddha, whereupon he led the assembly to establish a monastery and cast a statue of Great Compassion (Mahākāruṇika) forty-nine feet in height.
Prostrating himself before the image, he set forth his aspirations, saying: "The sacred form is now complete and the monastic hall is finished;
I pray that, by virtue of this holy power, I may soon ascend to the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (Sukhāvatī). In the middle of the night, he suddenly beheld a golden light.

Two rays of auspicious light appeared, with the Buddha and Bodhisattvas following them on the left and right. The Buddha extended his hand and took hold of Jue-shou, saying, "Fulfill your vow without wavering;
the benefit of sentient beings must come first. At the place where you are born in the Jewel Pond, your aspirations shall ultimately be realized.

Eleven years later, he saw a great deity emerge from the clouds with only half his body visible. The deity said to him, "The time for your rebirth in An-yang has arrived. Thereupon, before the image...
He passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture.

The National Preceptor Fazhao resided at Yunfeng Monastery in Hengzhou during the second year of the Dali era of the Tang dynasty (767 CE). Renowned for his compassion, forbearance, precepts, and meditative concentration, he was venerated by his contemporaries.
Once, while in the refectory, he beheld within his alms bowl a Brahma temple amidst clouds of five colors, situated directly to the east.
To the north, there was a mountain stream with a stone gate, and further on lay another temple whose title was inscribed in golden script: "The Great Sage’s Bamboo Grove Temple" (Dasheng Zhulin Si).
On another day, he again saw within his alms bowl several temples amidst the clouds, complete with ponds, terraces, and towers, where tens of thousands of bodhisattvas dwelt together.
The Master recounted what he had seen and consulted learned monks; two monks named Jiayan and Tanhui told him, "This is a holy [vision]."
The transformations of the divine are unfathomable by the emotions. If one discusses the topography and orientation of the mountains and rivers, it is indeed Mount Wutai.

In the fourth year, at Hudedong Temple in the prefecture, the Master held five assemblies for the recitation of the Buddha’s name (presumably one assembly per day). He was moved by the appearance of auspicious clouds that completely covered the sky.
Within the clouds were towers and pavilions; he beheld the body of Amitābha Buddha and two Bodhisattvas filling the void.

There were several Brahman monks walking along with their *khakkhara* staffs. He further saw an old man who said to him, "You previously made a vow to pay homage to the Great Sangha in the Golden Realm;
why have you now suddenly stopped? The Master then set out with his companions to travel far to Mount Wutai, where he saw [a sign] to the south of the temple.
Guang and his companions proceeded to Foguang Temple, where everything was exactly as he had seen within the bowl. Five li to the northeast, there was indeed a great mountain;
on the mountain was a ravine, and at the north of the ravine stood a stone gate flanked by two youths in blue robes—one named Sudhana and the other named Nanda.
The guide led him through the gate. Traveling north, he beheld golden gates and lofty towers; upon a golden plaque was inscribed: "The Great Sage’s Zhulin Monastery.
The monastery spanned twenty *li* square and contained one hundred courtyards, each featuring golden ponds, jeweled stupas, flowered terraces, and jade trees.
Entering the lecture hall, he saw Mañjuśrī to the west and Samantabhadra to the east, both seated upon lion thrones, preaching the Dharma for the assembly of Bodhisattvas.
They surrounded him in numbers in the tens of thousands. Before the two Bodhisattvas, the Master prostrated himself and asked:
"I do not yet know what Dharma-gate an ordinary person of the final age should practice. Mañjuśrī replied: "Among all gates of cultivation, none is equal to mindfulness of the Buddha.
The power of Amitābha Buddha’s vows is inconceivable; you should fix your mind upon it and resolutely seek rebirth there. At that time, the two Great Beings together extended [their hands].

The Golden-Armed One [Avalokiteśvara] stroked his head with his hand and bestowed upon him a prophecy, saying: "By the power of your mindfulness of the Buddha, you shall ultimately realize unsurpassed enlightenment.
Mañjuśrī spoke again: "You may proceed to the various monasteries of the bodhisattvas to tour them, pay homage, and receive their teachings.

The Master sought instruction from each of them in turn until he reached the Garden of Seven Jewels. He then returned once more before the Great Sage, prostrated himself, took his leave, and headed toward the two green peaks.
He sent his robes outside the gate; when the Master bowed again and looked up, they had both vanished.

Later, he went with fifty monks to the Vajra Cave—the place where Asanga had beheld the Great Sage—and suddenly beheld a palace of many jewels, with Mañjuśrī, Samantabhadra, ten thousand bodhisattvas, and Buddhapālita.
Just as the Master prostrated himself, he looked up and they immediately vanished. That night, at the Avataṃsaka Hall...
Seeing five-branched lamps on the cliffs and ravines to the east of the temple, the Master said, "I wish to divide these into a hundred lamps. Shortly thereafter, it was as he had wished.
He spoke again, saying, "I pray that they be divided into a thousand lamps," and the number likewise became so. The light pervaded the mountains and valleys.
Furthermore, he went before the Vajra Cave and at midnight beheld Buddhāpālita, who led him into the temple. Later, in the Huayan Hall, he meditated upon the two Great Beings.
He requested a prediction of his rebirth, whereupon he single-mindedly recited the Buddha’s name. Suddenly, he saw Boli, who said to him, "Your lotus pedestal has already been formed;
it will bloom in three years. When you see the various temples of the Bamboo Grove, why not let all sentient beings know of it?
The Master then commissioned artisans to carve a stone relief as a map and built Zhulin Temple at the site where he had seen it. Once it was completed, he addressed the assembly:
He said, "My work is finished. After several days, he sat apart from the assembly and passed away. Inferring from the words of Póli, it was indeed three years later.
The Master practiced the Five Assemblies in Bingzhou, teaching people to practice the recitation of the Buddha's name.

Emperor Dàizōng frequently heard the sound of reciting the Buddha's name coming from the northeast within the Chang'an palace. He dispatched an envoy to investigate it, who reached Tàiyuán and indeed saw the Master exhorting others.

The prosperity of his transformation was such that he was subsequently invited into the inner palace to teach the palace ladies to recite the Buddha’s name; this also extended to the Five Assemblies (wǔhuì), for which reason he was titled the Dharma Master of the Five Assemblies (Wǔhuì Fǎshī) and established as the Fourth Patriarch of the Lotus Society (Liánshè).
Dharma Master Shaokang was a native of Jin-yun Xian-du. His secular surname was Zhou, and his mother was of the Luo clan.
She dreamed that she traveled to Ding-hu Peak, where a jade maiden presented her with a blue lotus flower, saying, "This flower is auspicious; you shall give birth to a noble son.

When he was born, a green light filled the room and the fragrance of a lotus pervaded it. At the age of seven, he did not yet speak, which led physiognomists to marvel at him. His mother took him with her to...
At Ling Shan Temple, the Abbot pointed to the Buddha in the hall and asked him, "Do you revere the Buddha? He replied immediately, "Who would not revere Śākyamuni Buddha?
His parents were even more deeply impressed by his extraordinary devotion. They subsequently allowed him to renounce the household life.

At the age of fifteen, he had mastered five sections of the canon, including the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* and the *Śūraṅgama-samādhi-sūtra*. He then traveled to Jiaxiang in Kuaiji to study the Vinaya-piṭaka in depth. Later, he went to Shangyuan.

Longxing listened to various treatises such as the *Avataṃsaka* and the *Yogācāra*. In the first year of the Zhenyuan era of the Tang dynasty, while at Baima Monastery in Luoyang, he saw light emanating from the scriptures within the hall.
Upon examining them, he found they were the writings of the Venerable Shandao on the transformation and guidance toward the Western Pure Land. The Master said:
"If you have a karmic affinity for the Pure Land, I shall emit light once more. Having said this, the light flashed again.

The Master said, "Even if the kalpa-stone could be worn away, my vow shall never change. He then proceeded to the memorial hall of the Venerable Shandao at Guangming Temple in Chang’an, where he made extensive offerings.
Suddenly, the portrait of the deceased rose into the air and addressed him, saying, "If you rely upon my teachings, you shall widely transform sentient beings."

"Sentient beings! In days to come, when your merit is perfected, you shall surely be reborn in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (An-yang). Upon hearing these words from the Buddha, as if he had attained some realization, the Master traveled south to Jiangling.
On the road, he encountered a monk who said to him, "If you wish to transform sentient beings, you should go to Xin-ding (present-day Yanzhou). Having finished speaking, the monk vanished.
Once the Master had entered the commandery, no one recognized him. He then begged for money, luring small children by saying, "Amitābha Buddha is your teacher;
recite his name once and I will give you one coin. Those children who were intent on the coins would recite the name along with his voice.
After more than a month, many children were chanting the Buddha's name to seek money. The Master then said, "To those who can recite the name ten times, I shall give [one coin]."
[He] gave money. In this manner for one year, regardless of age or social status, everyone who saw the Master would chant "Amitābha Buddha.

The sound of reciting the Buddha’s name filled the roads. After ten years, he established a Pure Land practice hall at Mount Wulong. He constructed a three-tiered platform and gathered the assembly to perform the Way.
Whenever the Master ascended the seat, he would chant the Buddha’s name in a loud voice; the assembly then saw a Buddha emerging from [the light].
He spoke these words and uttered them ten times; as he chanted, ten Buddhas appeared before him. The Master said, "Since you have seen the Buddhas, you will certainly attain rebirth in the Pure Land.
At that time, among the several thousand people present, there were some who did not see them. Alas! They reproached themselves and redoubled their diligent practice.

On the third day of the tenth month in the twenty-first year, he entrusted his final instructions to Daoxuan, saying: "In the Pure Land, you should give rise to a heart of joyful aspiration; [in contrast], regarding Jambudvīpa..."
"Ti! Arise with a mind of weary detachment! You all are able to see this radiance at this moment; you are truly my disciples.

Thereupon, he emitted several rays of extraordinary light and departed. The people of the commandery built a stupa for him on the Taiyan cliff, calling him the Dharma Master of Taiyan, and the Lotus Society established him as the Fifth Patriarch.
Huaiyu was a person from Danshu. Wearing only plain clothes and eating but one meal a day, he remained constantly seated without lying down.
For nearly forty years, he visualized the Pure Land, reciting the names of the Buddhas fifty thousand times daily and chanting the *Amitābha Sūtra* three hundred thousand times.

In the first year of the Tiānbǎo era, he beheld Buddhas and Bodhisattvas filling the void; one person holding a silver platform came to welcome him. Yu said, "Throughout my life, I have focused my thoughts [on the Buddha]."
The Buddha vowed to take the golden platform, whereupon the holy assembly vanished. The Master redoubled his ascetic practices.

After twenty-one days, the person returned to him and said, "The Dharma Master has already attained rebirth in the highest grade. Suddenly, a wondrous light illuminated the room. Three days later, he wrote a verse:
"Pure and pristine, free from dust and defilement; Born by transformation upon a lotus flower as my parents. I have cultivated this for ten kalpas..."

The Way has arrived. He manifested in Jambudvīpa to exhaust the multitude of sufferings; through a lifetime of ascetic practice, he transcended ten kalpas. Forever leaving the Sahā world, he returns to the Pure Land.
His disciples saw the Buddha and Bodhisattvas together riding a golden terrace descend from the west to welcome him as he departed for the Jade Realm.
Duan Gong, the Prefectural Governor, composed a verse in praise: "In a single thought, my Master ascended to the First Stage; the songs and music of the Buddha-land [resound] in both directions."
He crossed over [to the Pure Land]. Only the ancient locust tree before his gate remained; its branches hung low, as if merely to support the golden platform.
Qi Han lived at Wupiu and entered the Lotus Water Buddha-Recitation Sanctuary. In the space of a single thought-moment, he beheld the景象 (manifestations) of the Pure Land.
Suddenly, he sang this verse: "The flowing water moves, its ripples shimmering; The lotus flowers reflect, their precious light shining."

Following [the light], he traveled westward on the rays; who was it that accompanied him? Ten years prior, when the Master was ill, his disciples asked, "Venerable Sir, as you are about to leave this life, why do you still harbor this illness?
The Master replied, "This body of mine must surely perish; even a sage cannot escape it. He then turned to gaze at the sacred image and passed away.

Shen Hao gathered monastics and laypeople in Wu Commandery to establish a Western Society (*xīfāng shè*). For those who were unable to cast off worldly burdens, he would lead them to withdraw from society.
At the time of his departure, he remarked, "In a sandalwood forest, common timber withers of its own accord. Later, manifesting illness, he said to his disciples:

"The auspicious signs of the Pure Land have already appeared; tonight I shall certainly be reborn there. Thereupon, he bathed his body, changed his robes, sat upright, and passed away, while a fragrant aroma filled the room.
Sengzang was a native of Xihe. During the summer months, while feeding mosquitoes among the grasses, he would recite the name of Amitābha Buddha for approximately twenty years.

Whether eating, drinking, walking, or sitting, his mind was always fixed upon the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (An-yang). Suddenly, amidst his illness, he beheld a transformed Buddha whose light illuminated his body.
The following day, he said to his attendant, "Just now, as I closed my eyes, I was precisely in the Pure Land. Various superior beings were scattering flowers and summoning me.
Thereupon, he adjusted his robes, faced west, and passed away.
Daheng entered Mount Tai to perform the Samantabhadra Repentance for three years. He was moved by the manifestation of the Great Being (Mahāsattva) before his eyes.

In his later years, he entered the Tripitaka chamber and expressed his aspiration; as he took up a scroll at random, he obtained the *Amitābha Sūtra*. Thereupon, he recited and chanted it day and night until the twenty-first day.
On the lapis lazuli floor, the Buddha and two great bodhisattvas appeared in person. Emperor Xizong heard of this event and issued an edict for them to enter the palace.
He bestowed upon him the title of Bodhisattva Constantly Diligent (Changjingjin) and enfeoffed him as Duke of Kaiguo. One year later, the lapis lazuli floor appeared once more.
On that very day, he passed away lying on his right side; a rare fragrance did not dissipate for ten days, and his physical body remained incorruptible.

Baoxiang resided in Chang’an for thirty years, performing prostrations and repentance rituals during the six periods of the day and night. He recited the *Amitābha Sūtra* seven times and chanted the Buddha’s name sixty thousand times.
Later, he suddenly saw the Buddha and a multitude of Bodhisattvas coming from the west to welcome him. He then instructed his disciples, saying:
Taking the practice of *nien-fo* (Buddha-recollection) as their primary vocation, they await one another in the Western Paradise.
The direct successor of Mazu Daoyi, known as Baizhang the Great Wise One, is revered by all monastic communities throughout the land.
When praying for the sick monks or performing the funeral rites for the deceased, they all turn toward the Pure Land as the means for their transcendence and deliverance.
Zhik’in specialized in the practice of meditation. He also recited the names of fifteen thousand Buddhas one hundred times.
Later, at the Aśoka Stūpa in Zhengzhou, he burned off one of his arms, vowing to be reborn in the Pure Land.
His disciple, Senghu, saw an extraordinary light illuminating the courtyard at midnight. He asked, “Who is holding a torch? He asked this three times, and a voice from the air replied, “I am coming.”

It was Master Yin who was being welcomed. As Hu hurriedly pushed open the window to look, he immediately beheld the radiance of the Buddha’s body, with banners, flowers, and jeweled canopies descending from the sky. At that very moment, Yin passed away.

Fashun followed the Du family. Whenever he traveled through various prefectures and states, he exhorted people to recollect Amitābha Buddha. He composed the "Text on the Five Repentances" and praised the Pure Land in verse.
When a disciple went to Mount Wutai, he saw an old man who said to him, "Mañjuśrī is currently residing at Mount Zhongnan."
This was the Venerable Dushun. When he returned [to his home], Shun passed away.
Huai-gan resided at Qianfu Monastery in Chang’an; after three years of buddha-recitation, he beheld the Buddha’s golden body and jade-like *ūrṇā*, and attained samādhi.
He then composed the seven-fascicle *Jueyi lun* (Treatise on Resolving Doubts). At the time of his death, he saw the Buddha come to welcome him, and he passed away with palms joined.

His virtue was renowned at the West Cloister of Huichang Temple, where he constructed a Hall of Repentance. Every year he practiced the *pratyutpanna-samādhi* (般舟), remaining seated throughout the summer retreat.

He sometimes restrained verbal transgressions, remaining silent for three years; or he practiced the *Bhadrakalpika-sūtra* (不輕), prostrating to all seven classes of followers. He also regulated his food and clothing.
He abandoned two of the four [elements], or else he eliminated the perception of the world and focused his mindfulness exclusively on the Western [Pure Land].
Reciting the name of Amitābha orally until the end of his life, at one time while entering his room, he called upon the Buddha and suddenly passed away.
Zhìtōng traveled to Mount Tiantai and, upon seeing Zhìzhě’s *Jìngtǔ yí* (Ritual for the Pure Land), his heart rejoiced in accord with its meaning.
Once, he went to Zhāoshǒu Yán (Waving-Hand Rock) and there made a great vow. Reciting the forty-eight vows of Amitābha Buddha, he finished his recitation and threw himself down from the rock.
A divine being caught him and placed him upon a tree; he then composed himself, climbed back onto the rock, and said: "This remaining life is weary; my great vow—"
Having already leaped forth, he was received and guided by the assembly of Bodhisattvas in the sea. He leaped down once more and landed upon thick, tangled grass.
After a long time, he regained consciousness; the monks of the monastery carried him back, and his body and mind were uninjured. Later, he traveled to Mount Fahuā in Yuè.
One night, he saw white cranes and peacocks flying in formation toward the west; lotus flowers opened and closed, and radiant signs appeared before him.
He then rose to prostrate to the Buddha and passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture.

Fashao resided in seclusion at Qiantang Huxin Temple, where he devoted himself exclusively to the recitation of the *Lotus Sūtra*, vowing that upon reaching ten thousand recitations, he would be reborn in the Pure Land.
One day, a lotus flower sprouted from the ground. Fashao vowed to immolate his body as an offering to the Three Holy Ones of the West;
however, King Chu of Wuyue earnestly exhorted him to desist. He then went to cast himself into the Cao'e River, where it was as if something supported him.
His feet were [crippled], yet a fisherman rescued him so that they did not wither. The King of Wu-Yue built a Pure Land Cloister at Baota Temple for him to dwell in.
One morning, he saw the light of a lotus flower illuminating his body; three days later, he joyfully passed away while seated.
Shouzhen was a native of Yongxing. He lectured on the *Qixin lun* (Treatise on the Awakening of Faith) and the *Fajie guan* (Contemplation of the Dharma Realm).

Regularly during the middle of the night, he would perform the secret mudrā for rebirth in the presence of Amitābha Buddha. When dawn was about to break, he would perceive himself ascending to the Pure Land;
opening his eyes, he beheld the Buddha. He would prostrate himself before the image and think: "If the Forty-eight Vows are able to deliver me," and then he would take up incense and flowers.
He entered the hall to offer worship and passed away while seated.
Wù'ēn was a native of Gūsū who resided at Cíguāng Monastery. He lectured on the *Lotus Sūtra* and various other scriptures. Later, he saw a white light emerge from a well;

thereupon, he abstained from food and recited the Buddha’s name. After three days had passed, he saw a monk from India holding an incense burner and circumambulating him three times, saying: "I shall bathe you."

He was the Venerable Ding. Because the practice you have cultivated accords with my own aspiration, I shall come from the Pure Land to welcome you. On the following day, En ascended the seat to preach on *śamatha* and *vipaśyanā*.
He pointed to his seat as his final destination and passed away while facing west. The assembly heard the sound of stringed and wind instruments in the air.
He departed westward, his destination indistinct.
Master Yitong was a native of Goryeo who resided at Baoyun Monastery in Siming. For nearly twenty years, he propagated the teachings of the doctrinal and contemplative schools (*jiaoguan*).
He habitually addressed others as "countrymen. When asked the reason for this, he said: "I regard the Pure Land as my true hometown; all of you should likewise do so."
They all attained rebirth [in the Pure Land] and were natives of my own hometown. Later, Zhi-li—also known as Fazhi—passed away while reciting the Buddha’s name in the right lateral position.

He resided at Nanhu and composed the *Miaozongchao*, a commentary on Tiantai Zhiyi’s *Guanjing shu* (Commentary on the Contemplation Sutra), which greatly elucidated the principles of contemplating the mind and contemplating the Buddha.
He once established an annual assembly for the practice of nianfo and the bestowal of precepts on the full moon of the second month.

The movement involved more than ten thousand people. He also compiled the *Rongxin jie* (Explanation on the Merging of Minds), which clarifies the three contemplations within the one mind and elucidates the meaning of the four pure lands.
Later, at the beginning of the year, he established a *Guangming chan* (Repentance of Radiant Light). On the fifth day, he summoned the great assembly to preach the Dharma;
after suddenly chanting the Buddha’s name several hundred times, he passed away while sitting upright.
Zunsui initially resided at Mount Dong on the eastern side of Tiantai, where he practiced the four kinds of samādhi extensively.

Later, he went to Baoyun Temple in Siming, where he gathered both monastics and laypeople to cultivate the Pure Land practice exclusively. He composed the *Record of the Vow for Rebirth in the Western Land*.

Subsequently, while residing at Ling Shan in Tianzhu, he constructed the Rizhuan Hermitage to the east of the temple as a place for the method of "sending the thought" toward the West; based upon the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra*, he composed the *Wangsheng Ji* (Record of Rebirth).

The Ritual for Repentance for Birth in the Pure Land was composed for Ma Liang, the Governor of Hangzhou, as a dharma-gate on the practices and vows for the Pure Land, along with a brief biography of those who attained rebirth there.
Later, while residing at Caotang, he manifested illness. When his disciples asked where he would be reborn, he replied, "The Pure Land of Tranquil Light.
At night, he suddenly passed away while sitting upright.
Youji studied under Baoyun and resided at Taiping Xingguo Temple. One day, manifesting illness, he extensively expounded the perfect meaning (*yuanzhi*) for his disciples.
Suddenly, the assembly saw light appear in the west and music resound through the air. The Master said, "Amitābha Buddha and the two Great Beings have personally arrived here.
He then passed away reclining on his right side facing west. His disciples subsequently dreamed of Amitābha...

He received a prediction of Buddhahood from the Buddha as the Tathāgata Cūḍāmaṇi. Alternatively, he dreamed that his teacher sat upon a blue lotus flower, holding a *cintāmaṇi* and preaching the Dharma to the Buddha.
Fazhi sighed and said: "To discuss the profound mysteries while lying ill and to behold the Buddha at the moment of death—this is truly worthy of reverence."
Benru, styled Shenzhao, resided at Mount Dongshan for thirty years. In addition to his lectures on the sutras, he gathered a hundred people to perform the Lotus Repentance for one year.
He formed the White Lotus Society with the Prefect, Lord Zhang Xun. One day, while ascending the seat to preach the Dharma, he took leave of the assembly.
Fishermen on the river saw a monk departing toward the west amidst the clouds. The following year, [the tomb] was opened...
The stupa’s sacred image appeared as if alive. A lotus flower grew before the stupa.
The Dharma Master Yanshou, whose courtesy name was Chongxuan, recited the *Lotus Sūtra* from his youth; he could read five lines at once and finished it in sixty days.
During the reign of the Qian family of Wuyue, he served as a tax collector and used official funds to purchase fish and shrimp to release them.
He was sentenced to execution by public display in the marketplace. The King of Wu-Yue sent someone to observe him, saying, "If his complexion changes, execute him;

if it does not change, spare his life. After a while, his complexion did not change, and thus he was granted his life. He subsequently went to the Chan Master Cuiyan of Siming to leave the household life.
He wore no silk or flossed cotton, and his food lacked rich flavors. He then went to visit National Teacher Shao, where he realized the essential point of the mind. The Master once said to him:
"You have a karmic affinity with the Original Master; one day you shall perform great Buddhist works, though I regret that I shall not live to see it.
He first went to Zhizhe Rock on Mount Tiantai, where he practiced meditative concentration for ninety days, during which time a crow nested in his robe. Later, at Guoqing Temple...
While performing the Lotus Sūtra Repentance, he saw a divine being enter carrying a halberd. The Master rebuked him, saying, "How dare you enter without permission?
The being replied, "Only those who have long accumulated pure karma reach this place. At midnight, while circumambulating the image, he saw Samantabhadra with a lotus flower in his hand.
He then ascended Zhizhe Rock and made two lots: one said, "Dwell in meditative concentration for life," and the other said, "Recite the sūtras."
He adorned the Pure Land with myriad virtues. Thereupon, he focused his mind in silent prayer and obtained the "Lot of Myriad Virtues" for reciting sutras; this occurred as many as seven times.
Thus, he devoted himself single-mindedly to the cultivation of pure karma and traveled to Tianzhu Peak in Jinhua, where he recited the sutras for three years.
During his meditative contemplation, he saw Avalokiteśvara pouring nectar into his mouth, whereby he attained eloquence. He first preached the Dharma at Xuedou.
In the first year of the Jianlong era, King Zhongyi invited him to reside at Lingyin. In the second year, he moved to Yongming (present-day Jingci).

He performed one hundred and eight daily practices, never failing them for even a moment. When students came to inquire about the Dharma, he took the mind as his primary tenet and awakening as his standard.
At sunset, he would go to a separate peak to practice the Way and recite the Buddha’s name; bystanders heard the sounds of conch shells and celestial music.
King Zhongyi said with joy, "From antiquity, there has never been one who sought the Western Paradise with such single-minded earnestness.
He then established for him the Xixiang Xiangyan Hall to fulfill his aspiration. During the fifteenth year of Yongming, he had one thousand seven hundred disciples;
he constantly conferred the Bodhisattva precepts upon the assembly, offered food to spirits and deities at night, and released living beings during the day.
He dedicated all [merit] toward the adornment of the Pure Land. At that time, people called him "Maitreya Descending to Birth.
On the twenty-sixth day of the second month in the eighth year of the Kaibao era, he rose at dawn, burned incense, addressed the assembly, and passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture.

He was posthumously granted the title Chan Master Zhijue. The Master’s Way spread beyond the seas; the King of Goryeo sent a letter and presented offerings, addressing him with the etiquette due to a disciple. The Master...

Since the three schools of Tiantai, Xianshou, and Cien possessed both points of agreement and difference, he invited their disciples who were knowledgeable in the Dharma to extensively read the ocean of meanings and engage in mutual debate. The Master used the standard of the Mind-essence school to level them out.

Furthermore, he compiled sixty Mahāyāna sūtras and śāstras, along with the words of three hundred masters from the two lands [China and India], to establish and verify the *Vijñaptimātra* (Consciousness-only) doctrine.

He compiled a hundred fascicles on the essential purport of the mind, titled *Zhongjing* (The Mirror of the Source). He also composed the *Wanshan tonggui ji* (Collection on the Ten Thousand Good Deeds Returning to the Same Source), which points the way back to the Pure Land and captures its most vital essence.
After the Master passed away, a stupa was erected for him in the mountains. A monk arrived from Linchuan and said:
While I was ill, I entered the underworld and was granted release. Upon my return, I saw a hall containing a statue of a monk. King Yama came in person and prostrated himself before it.
I asked who this figure was, and the presiding official replied, "This is Chan Master Shou of Hangzhou. Having heard of him, he has been reborn in the highest grade of the Western Paradise.
Because the King respects such a person, he pays his respects here. During the Chongning era, he was posthumously honored with the title Zong.
Master Zhao of the Chan school was designated as the Sixth Patriarch by the Lotus Society.
His posthumous name was Guangci. In his later years, he resided at the Leifeng Pagoda, where he recited the Buddha’s name without ceasing.

Suddenly, he dreamed that he entered a place resembling a palace, where someone told him, "The Middle Grade of the Pure Land is where you shall be reborn. He then saw another hall that was even more magnificent.
Her beauty was exquisite and peerless; people called her one born of the highest grade, destined to await the arrival of Chan Master Ben of Jingci Temple.
When she approached the end of her life, she indeed wrote a verse, sat cross-legged facing west, and passed away.
Siyi was styled Jinghui. He resided at Mount Ling for twenty-three years before retiring to Caotang. One day, he took his leave of the assembly and passed away.

After the assembly had been chanting for a long time, he suddenly returned to consciousness and said: "I have just followed the Great Being Avalokiteśvara and saw a golden-colored śramaṇa with a tall body and long arms.
He said to me: 'Your karmic conditions are not yet exhausted; after seven days have passed, I shall dispatch you.'"
He welcomed them. When the appointed time arrived, he sat in the lotus posture and passed away. On the day his stupa was buried, crimson clouds hung low, spreading toward the west before vanishing.
Yuanjing’s sobriquet was Biancai. Having resided at Upper Zhushan, he declined the position and lived at Longjing on South Mountain.

There he burned three fingers on the left and two on the right as an offering to the Buddha, devoting himself exclusively to the practice of the Pure Land contemplations. As death approached, he told his friend Daoqian: "My karma for the Western Paradise..."
He completed [his studies]. Seven days later he departed. When the appointed time arrived, he passed away peacefully on his right side.

Having studied under Tianzhu Haoyue (Sea-Moon), he recited the *Lotus Sūtra* five thousand times, the *Amitābha Sūtra* ten thousand times, and the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāpāramitā Sūtra* four thousand times, prostrating three times for every single character.
He performed the ritual circumambulation of the *Lotus Sūtra* three times; as for other sūtras, he recited them and paid homage without limit.

On the day of the *kṣaya* (the void), he vowed to be reborn in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (*An-yang*). His host, Yang Jie, composed thirty verses in praise of the Land of Bliss (*Anle guo zan*) as a gift for him.
Later, on the eighth day of the fourth month, he passed away while sitting cross-legged facing west; music resounded in the air, and a fragrance was perceived within his chamber.
When the fool resided at Xiantan in Zhachuan, he studied under Biancai and returned to the ocean of enlightenment.

He constructed a Pavilion of Immeasurable Life and exhorted both monastics and laypeople to practice mindfulness of the Buddha through seasonal assemblies for thirty years. As he was about to pass away, he dreamed that a divine being told him:
"Your fellow student, Zhi Zhang, has attained the Samādhi of Samantabhadra’s Practices and Vows and has already been born in the Pure Land; he is now waiting for you.

Thereupon, the Master bathed and changed his robes, commanding the assembly to recite the *Sutra on the Visualization of the Sixteen Contemplations*. After sitting upright and listening in silence until the end, he suddenly said:
"The Pure Land appears before me; I shall now depart. He suddenly wrote this verse and passed away: "Originally there is no home to which one can return; Who knows the path amidst the clouds?
The light of the stream falls afar upon the moon of the western mountains— This is precisely the moment the dream of the immortal pond ends.
Furthermore, half a month earlier, he had written another stanza: "A thousand-flower jeweled net in the void; Seven treasures within a dream."
Lianchi. Having firmly trodden the path back to the West, he was free from even a trace of doubt.
Zhishen, whose style name was Cixing, studied under Haiyue and returned to Jiahe, where he established the Changtang Hall and presided over it for twenty years.

He was single-mindedly devoted to the practice of Buddha-recitation and constantly used the Pure Land teachings to transform others. There were many who attained manifest signs of rebirth in the Pure Land through his guidance. One day, he manifested [his passing].
He fell ill. When a guest arrived to inquire after his health, they conversed as usual. Just as the guest was about to leave the door, the Master passed away.
Those who witnessed it saw purple clouds vanish toward the west.
Chuchu succeeded Shenzhao and resided at Bailian. One night, he gathered his disciples, prepared incense and flowers, and recited the *Bhadracaryā-praṇidhāna* and the *Amitābha Sūtra*.
Sitting upright, he extolled the merits of the Pure Land. He then addressed the assembly, saying, "I have attained the state of non-arising (*anutpāda*) many years ago.
Now, by means of non-arising, I shall be born in the Pure Land. As if entering a meditative absorption (*dhyāna*), he suddenly passed away.
He was thus transformed.

The Dharma Master named Shengchang, whose courtesy name was Zaowei, was surnamed Yan and was a native of Qiantang. At the age of seven, he grew weary of the mundane world; at seventeen, he received full ordination.
During the Chunhua era of the Song dynasty, he resided at Nan Zhaoqing Temple. Admiring the spirit of Mount Lu, he planned to establish a Lotus Society. To the west...

The lake is a supreme place for travel and recreation; it is where those who delight in noble seclusion find solace. It is here that one gazes with reverence toward the Buddha of Immeasurable Life and aspires to be reborn in his land.
Thus, he carved an image of the Buddha. Furthermore, the "Chapter on Pure Conduct" from the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* is the essential core for achieving sainthood;

thus, he transcribed it using blood drawn from his own body. Consequently, he changed the name of the Lotus Society to the "Society of Pure Conduct. All the gentlemen who joined the assembly were thereafter known as "Brothers of the Society of Pure Conduct."

My son, when the late Duke Wenzheng Dan served as the head of this society, for over thirty years there were more than thirty officials—ministers, dukes, and governors—who participated, numbering as many as one hundred and twenty-three.
Such was the success of its transformation. Now, with over a thousand fellow bhikṣus, the great assembly can see that West Lake is truly comparable to Mount Lu; it is not without reason. *Note:
The term "社首" (shèshǒu) refers to the head of a ritual association or society. The text describes the flourishing of a Buddhist community modeled after the White Lotus Society of Mount Lu.*
On the twelfth day of the first month in the fourth year of the Tianxi era, he sat upright reciting the Buddha’s name.

After a short while, he called out in a forceful voice, "The Buddha has come! and passed away peacefully. Those present saw the color of the ground turn entirely golden, which only faded after some time.
He was sixty-two years old. His disciples enshrined his whole body in a stupa beside the grave of Chan Master Niaoke. The Lotus Society established this as the seventh [memorial].
The Patriarch said:
"Chanshi Sixin Wuxin succeeded to the seat of Huanglong. His dharma influence was greatly revitalized, yet he was deeply intent upon the practice of pure karma;
he composed the 'Exhortation to Mindfulness of the Buddha' (Quan nianfo wen) to inspire others toward sorrowful repentance and the arousal of faith."
Zhenxie Qingliao succeeded Master Danxia Chun; thus, the lineage of the Dongshan school reached its greatest manifestation through him.
He established a hermitage on Mount Putuo and devoted himself exclusively to the Western Paradise, leaving behind the *Jingtu ji* (Collection on the Pure Land), which circulates in the world today.

Cishou Huashen received the Dharma from Master Xin of Changlu; he devoted his mind to the recitation of the Buddha’s name, asserting that no shortcut to cultivation surpasses rebirth in the Pure Land.
He established a Western Paradise practice hall and exhorted the assembly with earnest words.
Shizhi Zongxiao succeeded Yuetang Xun. He possessed a profound and penetrating mastery of the scriptural divisions and transformed others through the practice of Pure Land cultivation.
He once compiled various texts from the Great Canon, resulting in the *Lepang Wenlei* (Classified Writings on the Land of Bliss), which has been circulated in the world.
Jitang Yuansi and Miam Jie were both devoted practitioners of the *nien-fo san-mei* (Buddha-recollection samādhi).

Moved by their practice, a golden-armored deity descended from heaven, and in a dream, a red lotus flower emerged from the earth. Consequently, the Lotus School flourished throughout the Ten Continents.
Zongtan was a native of Luzhou and the son of the Shen family. At the age of sixteen, he took the tonsure under Master Daogong; for fifty years, his fame spread throughout the monastic academies.

In his later years, while at Qingtai Town in Tangzhou, he devoted himself exclusively to seeking rebirth in the Pure Land, never for a moment neglecting the three karmas or the four modes of deportment.
On the twenty-seventh day of the fourth month in the fourth year of the Zhenghe era, he dreamed of Amitābha Buddha, who said to him: "You..."
He preached the Dharma for six days and declared that he would be reborn in the Pure Land. Upon waking, he informed the assembly.

On the fourth day of the fifth month, he gathered the multitude and said, "The meeting and dispersing of causes and conditions must indeed have their appointed time; however, the supreme conditions for the Pure Land depend solely upon the moment.

I pray that you all recite the Buddha’s name to assist me in my rebirth. Having spoken, he passed away while seated. Thunder resounded throughout the sky, and white clouds covered the earth for three days.
He was just about to rest when the *mālā* of lapis lazuli he was holding slipped onto his finger. The crowd tried to remove it, but in the end they could not get it off.
His son’s courtesy name was Wanshi (All Matters Rest). His surname was Mao and his mother’s was Chai. She dreamed that a Buddha entered her door, and the next morning he was born;
thus he was named Fulai (Buddha-Come). His parents died early, and at the age of nineteen, he entered Yanxiang Temple under Master Zhitong to become a monk and practiced *śamatha*.
Guān was meditating one day when he heard the cry of a crow and attained enlightenment. He composed this verse: "For over twenty years I sought it upon paper;
Seeking and seeking, I grew ever more despondent. Suddenly I heard the cry of a compassionate crow, And only then did I believe my former efforts were in vain."

Thereupon, his altruistic resolve became most earnest. He universally exhorted others to practice mindfulness of the Buddha, performing prostrations and repentance on behalf of all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, and praying for rebirth in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (*An-yang*).

He established the White Lotus Repentance Hall and composed the *Four Lands and Three Contemplations* (*Si-tu San-guan*) and the *Selection of the Buddha-Diagram* (*Xuan-fo-tu*), revealing the essential eyes of the Lotus School.
He established the four-character phrase "Pujue Miaodao" (Universal Enlightenment, Wondrous Way) to define the name of his lineage. Emperor Gaozong summoned him for an audience.

He was bestowed the posthumous title of Cizhao. Later, at Duocheng on the twenty-third day of the third month, he addressed the assembly, saying, "My karmic conditions for transformation have come to an end;

it is time for me to depart. Having spoken these words, he joined his palms and entered nirvana. His remains were cremated, yielding countless relics, and by imperial decree, he was granted the Most Victorious Stupa (Zuisheng Ta).
Huaiyi was a native of Leqing, Wenzhou. His father made his living as a fisherman; when Huaiyi was young, he sat at the stern of the boat, catching fish alongside his father.

He would secretly throw the fish back into the water. His father grew angry and beat him, yet Huaiyi felt no regret. He subsequently took leave of his parents and entered the monastic life at Jingde Temple.

During the Tiānshèng era, he passed the scriptural examinations and received full ordination. He received the Dharma from Chan Master Xuán of Cuìfēng. He presided over five monasteries in succession, solely for the purpose of transforming others.

While the assembly was recollecting the Buddha, someone offered instruction on the practice of the Pure Land. On the evening of his passing, his disciple Zhicai asked, "The construction of the stupa is now complete;
what is the ultimate matter? The Master raised his fist to show him, pushed aside his pillow, and passed away.

Zhìyuán resided at Gushan on West Lake. He provided extensive commentaries on various sutras and devoted his mind to the Pure Land. He composed the *Amitābha Commentary* (*Mítuō Shū*) and the *Western Aid Excerpts* (*Xīzī Chāo*) to encourage rebirth in that realm. When his end approached, he passed away while sitting upright. His remains were interred within a pair of earthenware jars. Fifteen years later, [The text continues: ...a stupa was erected for him. One night, a monk dreamed of Zhìyuán, who said, "I have been reborn in the Western Land. Upon waking, the monk investigated the matter and found it to be true. Thereafter, many people believed in the Pure Land teachings because of this. It is said that Zhìyuán had once told his disciples, "When I die, bury me in an earthenware jar; do not erect a stupa. His disciples did as he instructed. Later, when the stupa was built, they opened the jar and found his body intact, with no sign of decay. It was as if he had merely fallen asleep. This was truly a manifestation of the power of the Pure Land. It is recorded that in the year Wucheng (1024) of the Zhenzhong era, Zhìyuán was seventy-nine years old. He had been a monk for fifty-five years. His secular surname was Chen, and he was a native of Yuhang County. He was a descendant of the lineage of the former Prince of Jingling. His father, Zhìyuan, was a man of great virtue. Zhìyuán’s mother dreamed of a golden statue entering her womb, after which she conceived him. From childhood, he possessed extraordinary intelligence and was naturally inclined toward the Way. At age seven, he entered the monastic order under Master Huìshān of the Dàchéng Temple in Yuhang. At eighteen, he received full ordination. He traveled extensively to visit eminent masters and studied the profound and subtle teachings of the Tripitaka. He was particularly skilled at expounding the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*. Later, he went to the capital, where he studied under Master Fǎzàng of the Huázhāi Temple. Fǎzàng highly praised his talent. Subsequently, he returned to the West Lake region, where he lived in seclusion at Gushan. He lectured on the *Lotus Sūtra* and the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*, and his reputation spread far and wide. He also lectured on the *Vimalakīrti Sūtra* and the *Śrīmālādevī Siṃhanāda Sūtra*. His followers numbered in the thousands. He was deeply devoted to the Pure Land and constantly recited the name of Amitābha Buddha. He also wrote the *Pure Land Verses* (*Jìngtù Jù*). His life was one of constant diligence, and he never neglected his practice. He passed away peacefully at his residence on Gushan. His disciples followed his instructions and buried him in an earthenware jar. After his death, his fame continued to grow, and many people were inspired to seek rebirth in the Pure Land. Thus, the teaching of the Western Paradise flourished through his efforts. It is said that the stupa containing his remains still stands today. Those who visit it find it a place of solemn beauty, a testament to his spiritual legacy. His disciples maintained the tradition of his teachings, ensuring that his influence would endure for generations. His works, including the *Amitābha Commentary* and the *Western Aid Excerpts*, remain central texts for practitioners of the Pure Land school. Through his dedication and wisdom, Zhìyuán played a pivotal role in the propagation of the faith in the Land of Ultimate Bliss. After heavy rains, a mountain collapsed. Upon opening the view of a ceramic vessel, the physical form remained intact, though the nails and hair had grown long.
Sengzang was a native of Fenzhou who, throughout his life, did not accept prostrations from either monastics or laypeople, devoting himself exclusively to the practice of Pure Land.

As he approached his end, celestial music came in succession to welcome him, yet he declined to go with them all. When the Buddha of the Western Paradise arrived, he passed away separately from the assembly.

Yanyan received the teachings at Mount Lingjiu of Tiantai, following the lineage of Shenzhao and Zhizhe. In his later years, he resided at Zhua-an, where he devoted himself exclusively to the practice of Pure Land Buddhism.

He composed four poems titled "Longing for the Native Land of An-yang," which were widely circulated at the time. After ten years living in the mountains, he dreamed of a great lotus flower in a pond with celestial music arrayed on all four sides;
thereupon, he composed "Poems on Departing for the Pure Land. Seven days later, he sat in the full lotus posture and passed away.
He passed away, and a light like the moon emanated from atop his stupa; it remained for three nights before fading.
He was posthumously titled Mingzhi (Wisdom-Enlightened). Residing at Nanhu, he constantly exhorted others toward the practice of pure karma (*śubha-karma*).

His disciple Jie’er established the Hall of the Sixteen Contemplations (*ṣoḍaśa-vipaśyanā-śālā*), which became the foremost in the eastern provinces; this was truly due to the Master’s encouragement. One night, he said to his attendant: "Now..."

She smelled a rare fragrance and felt her mind was deeply at ease. She immediately summoned those from the meditation hall, and when everyone had gathered, she spoke with a smile, saying, "The time for my rebirth has arrived.
She then sat facing west and passed away.

Zhai Ying was a native of Tongjiang. Relying upon the sutras and śāstras, he distinguished between the two types of cultivation—the specific and the general—to demonstrate the ease of rebirth in the Pure Land.
He also composed the *Jingtuxiuzhengyi* (Ritual for Cultivation and Realization in the Pure Land) in two fascicles, which circulated in the world.

The verse currently known as "The True Golden Color of Amitābha Buddha" was written by this master. One night, he fell ill; facing west and leaning against a desk, he recited the Buddha’s name and passed away.
Sizhao received the precepts at Jingzhu Monastery in Qiantang. He drew blood to transcribe the *Lotus Sūtra*, performing one prostration for each character;
he did this ten times. He recited the *Sūtra of the Sixteen Contemplations* five hundred times, the *Amitābha Sūtra* one thousand times, and the *Lotus Sūtra* one thousand times.

He also paid homage to seven scriptures, including the *Avataṃsaka*, the *Brahmajāla*, and various Pure Land sūtras, totaling two hundred and seventy fascicles. Every night at the fourth watch, he would...

He rose and said, "Those who are indolent in their mindfulness of the Buddha, upon hearing this voice, were struck with awe and shame. Furthermore, on the twenty-third day of every month, he led both monastics and laypeople to focus their minds on the Three Sages;
the assembly regularly reached a thousand people. This continued until the end of the Master's life, spanning thirty years in total.

One night, he spoke to his disciples, saying, "In a dream last night, I saw the golden body of the Buddha, sixteen feet in height. Is this not a sign that my rebirth in the Pure Land is imminent? Thereupon, he requested [the assembly] to do so daily.
Seven monks assisted him in reciting the Buddha’s name. On the evening of the seventh day, he rose from his seat, joined his palms, and recited the Buddha’s name with a forceful voice.
Sitting cross-legged and forming mudrās, he passed away.

Zongli received his precepts at Tianhua Monastery in Kuaiji. He practiced the Lotus Repentance for three years. In a dream, his deceased mother thanked him, saying, "I owe my rebirth in a good realm to the merit of your repentance.
When the period was complete, he saw Samantabhadra passing through the air. He then visited Dazhi Vinaya Master to further receive the rules of discipline.
Suddenly, he dreamed that the Vinaya Master spat out a white pearl and commanded him to swallow it. He once experienced a divine journey to the Pure Land.
On the earth, he beheld the appearance of jeweled ponds, lotus flowers, and rows of trees.

He then proceeded to a new city with emerald ponds, where he practiced the *nien-fo san-mei* (Buddhānusmṛti-samādhi) for ten years. Later, he entered Daowei Mountain and built a hermitage named Yixiang (One Appearance).
After fifteen years had passed, he said to his disciples, "I see white lotus flowers filling the sky. Three days later, he said again, "The Buddha is coming," and immediately wrote:
The verse says: "I am ninety years old, my hair is white as snow; there should be no guests remaining in this world for a hundred years. You who possess the marks of a sage, return!
When you sit upon the golden terrace, heaven and earth will seem narrow. He then passed away suddenly.
Qi Yu’s dharma name was Huijue. Initially, at Baozang Monastery in Xiachuan, he established a Pure Land assembly; those who recited the Buddha’s name were as numerous as ants.
Later, while residing at Upper Zhuhong, he would carry an image of Amitābha on his head at midnight and practice walking meditation while reciting the Buddha’s name.
One day, he said to the head seat: "A many-treasured stupa has appeared before my bed; this is not what I seek. What I wish to see is Amitābha Buddha."
"You may assemble the monks for me to practice *nianfo*. Let the Head Seat strike the bell for the *xiannian* (commemoration) service.
After about a hundred people had gathered, he said, "I have now seen the Buddha," and immediately closed his eyes, sat upright, and passed away.

Zhongmin’s *Collection of the Principles of the Teachings* (Jiaoyi xianzhang ji) records that he was a native of Sanqu. While studying under Master Xiangfu, he ascended the lion throne and beheld a silver altar appearing from the west.
The master said, "Throughout my life, I have expounded the primary meaning [of the Dharma] and vowed to attain the Golden Terrace;
yet now it has come to this. He passed away on that very seat.

Yingke studied under Yaoshan of Xichuan. He traveled extensively to consult the various monastic seats of both the Exoteric and Esoteric traditions. Due to illness, he returned to his place of study, where he consumed wine and roasted meat without discrimination.

Reflecting privately that his precepts and karma were deficient, and fearing he might continue to wander through the cycle of rebirth, he had his fellow resident retrieve the *Biographies of Rebirth in the Pure Land* compiled by Master Jiezhu.
They read them together by their bedside; for every biography they read, they gained a point of deep conviction.
Thereupon, he selected a room and arranged a meditation chair facing west. For three days, he abstained from food and recited the Buddha’s name.
In a dream, the Buddha and the Great Beings (Bodhisattvas) said to him, "You still have ten years of life remaining; you should exert yourself.

Huikuo replied to the Buddha, "Even if I were granted a hundred years, this world of Jambudvīpa is turbid and evil, making it easy to lose right mindfulness. My wish is to ascend early to the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (Sukhāvatī) to serve the assembly of sages. The Buddha...
He said, "If your resolve is such as this, I shall come to welcome you in three days. When the appointed time arrived, he instructed the assembly to recite the *Amitābha Sūtra*.
The Master said, "The Buddha and the Great Assembly have all arrived," and then he passed away peacefully.
Lingzhao resided at Chaoguo on Huating. Every year she held a Pure Land assembly lasting seven days, during which time the monastics and laypeople often numbered twenty thousand.
In a dream, she saw the Three Holy Ones; she knelt and asked them, "I, Lingzhao, have spent my entire life hoping to be reborn in An-yang (Sukhāvatī).
Will this vow be fulfilled? Avalokiteśvara pointed to her and said, "The Pure Land is not far; if you have the vow, you shall be born there immediately. One day, while lying ill, she said:
The attendant said, "My time for rebirth is near. He then sat facing west in the full lotus posture and passed away.
Ke lived for a long time at Siming Kaihua Temple, where he constantly recited the *Lotus Sūtra*.

Because he had passed away while sitting, he revived after three days and spoke of matters concerning the Pure Land, which did not differ from the *Sūtra on the Visualization of the Buddha of Infinite Life*. He saw lotus pedestals, each bearing the names of those destined to be born there.
One purple-gold platform was inscribed: "Dharma Master Xun of the Guangjiao Monastery in Chengdu, Great Song, shall be reborn here.
Next, a gold platform read: "The Dharma Master Jiu of Mingzhou shall be reborn here. Another gold platform read: "The lay devotee Sun Shier of Mingzhou shall be reborn here.
Furthermore, a silver platform was inscribed: "The Daoist nun Xu of Mingzhou shall be reborn here."
In this regard, after he had finished speaking, he passed away. Five years later, the nun Xu died; a wondrous fragrance filled the room. Twenty years later, Layman Sun passed away;
celestial music filled the sky, moving the people of the entire commandery so that they all came to attend his funeral.
Zongben first studied under Chan Master Tianyi Huai and attained realization. Later, he resided at Jingci Monastery and, by imperial decree, entered Huilin Monastery in the Eastern Capital.
He was summoned for an audience at the Yanhe Hall, where he privately cultivated the practices of the Pure Land. At the time of his death, he passed away while sitting peacefully.
Dharma Master Cairen of Leifeng traveled spiritually to the Pure Land and saw a magnificent hall, where a person said, "This is to await the Pure [Land]."
Chan Master Ciben, as well as Master Xi of Zifu, went to Hui-lin Temple, prostrated themselves at his feet, and departed after making an offering of gold.
When others questioned them about this, they replied: "In meditative concentration, I saw golden lotuses with human faces, saying they were to await Chan Master Ben of Hui-lin.
Furthermore, there were countless small lotuses, which were said to be for those awaiting ordination. Some of them were withered, which was said to signify their falling away from the path."

This man was one who had attained ordination through his successful recitation of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra. Following his tenure at Jingci Monastery, he was summoned by imperial decree to reside at Fayun Monastery, where he was granted the title "Great Penetration" (Dàtōng).

Later, he returned to Xiàngǔ in Hangzhou, where he devoted himself exclusively to the practice of Pure Land cultivation. During his meditation, a monk beheld Amitābha Buddha manifesting before the abbot’s quarters.

His body was golden in color. One day he told his disciples, "Only three days remain. When the time arrived, he sat in the lotus posture facing west and passed away. Yuanzhao resided at Lingzhi Monastery;

while he propagated the study of the Vinaya, he devoted particular attention to the practice of Pure Land. One day he gathered his disciples and recited the *Guan wuliangshou jing* (Contemplation Sutra).
He passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture amidst the *Sūtra* and the "Universal Worthy’s Vows. Fishermen at West Lake all heard the sound of music in the air.
Daoyan was a native of Kuaiji and a senior disciple of Lingzhi; he specialized in the practice of Pure Land. Several days before his death, he saw...

Two divine beings, over ten feet tall, appeared and asked, "Why do you not fix your mindfulness? Thereupon, the monastics and laypeople assembled in a great gathering and practiced the Buddha-recitation for three days and nights.
As it neared its conclusion, [the Master] ascended the seat himself and preached the Dharma, performing repentance on behalf of the assembly. At evening, he passed away while seated.
The Dharma Master Zongze, styled Cijue, was a native of Xiangyang. He left the household life under Chan Master Xiu of Changlu Temple.
His vows were vast and profound, and he attained deep insight into the principles of Chan. During the Yuanyou era, he invited his aged mother to reside in the eastern chamber of the abbot’s quarters.

He exhorted her to practice mindfulness of the Buddha with diligent perseverance; for seven years, they did so without interruption. When his mother approached the end of her life, she indeed passed away peacefully and without illness. The Master continued to cultivate himself with great diligence.
To transform sentient beings, he followed the regulations of Mount Lu and established the "Supreme Assembly of the Lotus.
The method was to recite the name of Amitābha Buddha daily—whether a hundred times, a thousand times, or ten thousand times—and to mark each instance with a cross beneath the day.

One night, he dreamed of a youth wearing a black cap and white robes, of refined and beautiful countenance, who informed the Master that he wished to enter the Lotus Assembly and requested a written record. One...

His name was Ze. When he took up his brush to inquire after [the Master’s] name, [the Master] replied, "Puhui. He further said, "My elder brother Puxian also requests to be appended to this record," and then withdrew.
The Master Jue said to the senior monks, "In the 'Chapter on Leaving the World' of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, there are two bodhisattvas, Puxian and Puhui, who assist in propagating the Buddha-dharma.
Now, together with the great assembly, we shall gather to practice mindfulness of the Buddha, vowing to be reborn in the Pure Land, relying upon the grace of these sages."

The Venerable [Master] was included among those whose deeds were recorded in the *Youzan lu* (Records of Subtle Assistance), where he was ranked first among the two Great Beings (*mahāsattva*). Far and near, people turned toward his transformation.

He composed one hundred and twenty verses of the *Zuochan zhen* (Admonition on Seated Meditation) and the *Quanxiao wen* (Text Exhorting Filial Piety), as well as the *Shouquan jingtu song* (Verses Exhorting the Cultivation of the Pure Land).
In it, he said: "The three realms blaze like a mass of fire; for a practitioner, they are not yet a place of rest. The lotus pond awaits its virtuous friends for a long time; gather up your body..."

May your heart be inclined to return [to the Pure Land]. Let your eyes visualize and your mind dwell upon the sacred countenance of the Sage; you must simply maintain this moment by moment without giving rise to doubt.
When the flowers bloom in the Pure Land in years to come, remember the time you recited the Buddha’s name in this Sahā world.

Regarding Linji (Lin-chi) who recited the Buddha’s name while sitting as he passed away, Master Zhao of Lingzhi hailed him as a Great Vehicle teacher of recent times. Furthermore, the Lotus Society established him as one of its Eight Patriarchs.
Yueju resided at Huicheng Monastery, where he was renowned for his mastery of the Vinaya and his cultivation of the Pure Land practices. One day, an extraordinary monk came to welcome him.

Two days later, he fell slightly ill; he urgently called his fellow practitioner Daoning and said, "I now see Amitābha Buddha, who is eight feet tall and stands suspended in mid-air. Having spoken these words, he passed away.
Siming relied upon divine fungi. Having once received the precepts, he devoted himself single-mindedly to pure practices for twenty years.

One day, he fell ill and invited the assembly to recite the *Amitāyurdhyāna Sūtra* for half a month. On the third day, he saw transformation Buddhas filling his room. At the time of his death, as he recited the Buddha’s name, his voice carried beyond the hall.
During the intense heat of summer, his coffin was kept open; for seven days it remained unchanged, and a wondrous fragrance wafted forth.
Xingxun recited the *Sifen lü jieben* (Four-Part Vinaya Manual) and mastered it in three days. He studied the Vinaya under Dazhi and resided at Mingqing Temple for twenty years.
Once, while suffering from an illness, he prepared an image and instructed his disciples to maintain focused mindfulness for several days. Suddenly, he rose and asked for his three monastic robes;
he then chanted the *Amitābha Sūtra* and recited the Buddha’s name with a forceful voice. Sitting in the full lotus posture, he passed away.

Fachih resided at Huadu Temple, where he practiced the Amitābha Repentance for three years until two of his fingers were consumed by the flames. He further received the precepts and fashioned images of the Three Sages of the Western Paradise.
He recited the *Amitāyurdhyāna Sūtra*, the *Amitābha Sūtra*, and the *Rucigati-cakra-dhāraṇī*, vowing to shorten his life in Jambudvīpa so that he might be born early in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.

One day, while suffering from a slight illness, he wept with intense grief and made a fervent plea, praying that [the Buddha] would grant him a welcoming descent and lead him forth. He focused his mind on...
The Buddha’s voice was heard at a distance of a hundred paces. Suddenly, he saw the Buddha’s body, sixteen feet tall, standing upon the pond.
He then said to himself, "I have attained rebirth in the middle grade. He sat upright facing west and passed away.

Huìhēng resided at Yǎnshòu Monastery in Wúlín; his style name was Qīngzhào. He followed Língzhī to study the Vinaya and devoted himself exclusively to the practice of Pure Land for nearly sixty years.

Whenever he encountered guests or friends, he invariably exhorted them to recite the Buddha’s name. He constructed a precious pavilion and established images of the Three Sages, which were considered most extraordinary.
The high official Jiāng Zìrèn always held him in deep respect. One day, the Master suddenly dreamed that a jeweled throne descended from the void.

Below it says: "The Vinaya Master Qingzhao was to ascend this seat. When his fellow practitioner, Layman Sun, informed him that the Master had recently departed, having passed away while at home making seals, the Master went to offer incense. Upon returning, he said to his disciples: 'Master Sun has already gone.'"
"I, too, shall now depart. He then invited the assembly to recite the Buddha's name. He further said, "Recite the name of Amitābha with every word;

contemplate and hold it in mind at every thought. This is the mind of non-retrogression; one will certainly be born in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing. Having spoken thus, he sat upright and passed away.

Yongqin resided at Qibao Monastery in Qiantang, where he studied the Vinaya under Dazhi. He heard Dazhi address the assembly, saying: "If one propagates the *vinaya* while alive, one shall return to An-yang (Sukhāvatī) upon death;
for those who leave the household life to seek the Way, their primary task is hereby complete. Thereupon, Yongqin set his mind upon the Pure Land with single-minded resolve that never wavered.
He recited the Buddha’s name daily up to thirty thousand times. Once, while his spirit traveled to the Pure Land, he beheld the Great Being (the Buddha) in various manifestations.
Regarding his passing, he said to his attendant, "I shall travel west tomorrow. He immediately gathered the assembly to recite the Buddha's name.
At dawn, with palms joined, he gazed toward the west and passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture.
Miaosheng was a native of Kuaiji. He studied the Vinaya and daily practiced the discipline of the Pure Land.
Together with Chan Master Dàtōng Běn, he resided at Xiàngǔ on Cháoshān, where they jointly elucidated this Way.

One night, having gathered his disciples to recite the *Amitābha Sūtra*, he sat upright upon his couch, took up the incense intended for his passing and burned it, joined his palms in greeting, and passed away in a state of serene stillness.
Weiwo was a native of Qiantang. He retired from public life and secluded himself at home, where he read the Tripitaka three times;

including the *Avataṃsaka* and *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* sūtras, the total amounted to twenty thousand scrolls. In his later years, he recited the *Amitābha Sūtra* twenty times through the entire canon. One evening, he suddenly fell ill;
facing west, he sat upright, formed the meditative seal, and passed away.
